body: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated multilingual capabilities across diverse language generation and understanding tasks. Yet effective code-switching requires more than multilingual proficiency: models must decide when, where, and why to switch languages in ways that fit the surrounding context. This context-sensitive ability remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce CSWBench, a benchmark for evaluating context-sensitive code-switching in creative writing through two complementary settings: Focused Narrative and Extended Narrative. We further propose CSWEval, a theory-informed framework with two complementary levels: event-level evaluation of Licensing, Contextual Appropriateness, and Functional Gain, and whole-text evaluation of task-specific quality---overall literary and narrative quality in Focused Narrative and quality emphasizing multilingual organization in Extended Narrative. Evaluating twelve LLMs, we find that models exhibit meaningful but uneven code-switching competence across narrative contexts. Model differences are particularly pronounced in multilingual literary integration, while multilingual-focused dimensions show stronger difficulty effects overall than the general narrative dimensions; narratively salient switches are associated with stronger contextual and functional realization; and event-level CS quality is moderately associated with whole-text performance.
summaryZh: 本文介绍了CSWBench，这是一个专门用于评估大模型在创意写作中语境敏感代码转换能力的基准测试。研究通过“聚焦叙事”和“扩展叙事”两种设置，结合CSWEval评估框架，从事件级（许可性、语境适宜性、功能增益）和全文本级对十二款大模型进行了深入测评。结果显示，模型在多语言文学整合能力上存在显著差异，且多语言相关维度的评估难度高于通用叙事维度。该基准为理解模型在复杂多语言语境下的表现提供了量化依据，揭示了模型在叙事连贯性与语言切换逻辑上的潜在短板。
